solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Star female curiously the source of daughter's frailty

indicators.note: curiously means in a strange, odd way, so the letters that follow are arranged oddly

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter, followed by the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A clue that seems to ask which woman first brought weakness on her daughters, as Eve is said to have done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' rearranges DS plus FRAILTY. 'the source of' only links the definition to the anagram, though it also hints at Eve, the first woman, whose fall is blamed for human frailty.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife of a president is the nation's leading woman, so a star female in public life.

clue.text: Extract coming from revolutionary manuscript

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning right round, so the letters of the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: an extract such as an essential oil is a concentrated essence
of means coming from, as in a man of Kent

explanation.surface: It reads as a passage quoted from a manuscript by some revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extract' looks like the definition, but the manuscript is what is defined; 'revolutionary' turns the wordplay round.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf or large sheet of a handwritten book is called by this name, standing for the manuscript itself.

clue.text: Return of old woman to heave boxes

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the piece for heave goes round the piece for old woman

parts.note: to heave is to retch, to try to vomit
a mother, informally MA, is someone's old woman

explanation.surface: It pictures an old woman coming back and being sick into some boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' here is the noun: a return game.
explanation.definitionFit: A return in sport is a second contest between the same sides, a replayed fixture.

clue.text: Dress down, and start liking one's job?

definitions.meaning: to dress someone down is to scold them severely
read literally: to take to a task is to begin to enjoy one's work

explanation.surface: It seems to ask whether casual clothing at work makes people start to enjoy their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for scolding is read literally as warming to one's work; the question mark flags that whimsical second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to rebuke or reprimand; read word by word it means beginning to like one's assigned work.

clue.text: Fussy hosts ultimately plan events for the year

indicators.note: hosts means holds within, so the fussy word takes another letter inside it

parts.note: anal, short for anal-retentive, means fussy and obsessive about detail

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of plan is used

explanation.surface: A fastidious host meticulously schedules the year's social calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: A record of a single year's happenings, as in a chronicle kept year by year, gives one entry of history.

clue.text: After work, delay for a long drink

indicators.note: after being worked, the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone puts off going home after work in favour of a long drink at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After work' sounds like a time of day but is the anagram signal for DELAY FOR A.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall trumpet-shaped glass about three feet high, holding over two pints of beer, makes a literally long drink.

clue.text: Good person not in fairness displaying energy

indicators.note: not in says one piece is left out of the other

parts.note: justice is fairness, fair treatment
ST, short for saint, is the crossword's usual good person

explanation.surface: It seems to describe someone showing vigour in the absence of a good person's sense of fairness.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for electrical power or fuel, and so for energy in general.

clue.text: Finishes off twin projects, displaying extraordinary power

indicators.note: twin means a pair, so the shortened word appears twice
finishing a word off means cutting its final letter

parts.note: to project is to stick out, to jut

explanation.surface: Someone completes a pair of projects and shows remarkable ability.
explanation.definitionFit: A West African word for the supernatural force attributed to a charm or fetish, so magical power.

clue.text: One to drop off packs left one set on pedestal

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: packs means holds inside, so the sleep word takes two letters within it

parts.note: to drop off is to fall asleep, to doze
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A courier dropping off packages leaves one placed on a stand.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone on a pedestal is to worship or adore them excessively.

clue.text: Wrong RE student committed

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are in the wrong order and must be put right

explanation.surface: A student of religious education has been mistakenly locked away.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is religious education, a British school subject; here it is simply anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Committed in the sense of handed over for safekeeping, as when a duty is given to someone's care.

clue.text: Ducks out of strike: bravo, folks!

definitions.note: here a term of endearment, singular in sense though it ends in s

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or strike hard
Bravo is B in the NATO phonetic alphabet
your folks are your kin, your relatives

explanation.surface: A union boss calls off a strike with a cheer to the workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ducks' is a British affectionate form of address, like 'dear', not birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A little lamb, used as a pet name for a darling, matching the British endearment.

clue.text: Member of military caste turned to work — shock!

indicators.note: turned means reversed, so the pieces are read from right to left

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work
a jar is a jolt or shock

explanation.surface: A soldier from a warrior caste returns to work after a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: An older spelling of Rajput, a member of a Hindu warrior caste of northern India.

clue.text: Where French gallery with large arch is looking shabby

parts.note: ou is French for where
the Tate is the famous London art gallery
a bow is a curve or arch

explanation.surface: A French art gallery with a big arch has become run down.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from sleeves worn through at the joint of the arm, meaning ragged or down at heel.

clue.text: Remain confined to bed, missing quiet place

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: to lie up is to stay in bed through illness
P, for piano, is the musical notation for quiet

explanation.surface: A patient told to stay in bed misses a quiet place.
explanation.definitionFit: Used in the phrase 'in lieu of', it means stead or place.

clue.text: Festival with popular songs in German and ever poetic

parts.note: hits are popular songs
und is German for and
ay, or aye, is a poetic word for ever

explanation.surface: A festival featuring pop songs in German and some poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian feast of Pentecost, seventh Sunday after Easter, a church festival.

clue.text: Remove cap? That honour regularly goes to the Left

indicators.note: going to the left means moving leftward, read back to front in an across entry
regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter

explanation.surface: Someone doffs a cap as an honour passes to a left-wing politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks T, A, H, N, U from THAT HONOUR, and 'goes to the Left' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking off one's hat; the query flags that a cap is a type of hat.

clue.text: Lead attack on journalist after United criticised

indicators.note: after means placed later in the answer, so these pieces follow the one for United

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
a raid is an attack
ED, editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A football report of United leading an attack and a journalist being criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold or reproach someone angrily, a synonym of criticise.

clue.text: Shatters convertible at maximum speed in this?

definitions.text: Shatters convertible at maximum speed in this?

parts.note: c is the physics symbol for the speed of light, the greatest possible speed

indicators.note: convertible means able to be changed, so these letters are converted into a new order

explanation.surface: A soft-top car is smashed when driven flat out in a safety trial.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: a trial in which a car is driven fast and wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety trial in which a vehicle is deliberately smashed into a barrier to measure damage.

clue.text: A lot of passengers in train see notice

parts.note: to train is to coach
lo is an old word meaning look, see
an ad, advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: Many passengers on a train see an announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' is the verb to coach, not the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A busload of travellers, the number carried by one motor coach.

clue.text: Champion's speed is key

parts.note: read as the verb champions, meaning supports or backs
pace is speed

explanation.surface: A sports pundit says a champion's speed is what matters most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like an adjective meaning crucial, but it is a keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer keyboard button that deletes the character before the cursor.

clue.text: Cautious when circling naval officer's bedstead

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: chary means wary, cautious
PO, petty officer, is a naval rank

explanation.surface: A naval officer is wary of a bed frame.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian light bed with a frame strung with webbing or tape, so a bedstead.

clue.text: Short article: one way to get a degree

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: the is the definite article
I is the Roman numeral for one
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A student wonders whether a short essay could earn them a degree.
explanation.walkthrough: In British universities degrees are graded first, upper and lower second, and the lowest class of honours.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest class of British honours degree, a qualification on graduating.

clue.text: State of record company endlessly attracting gossip

indicators.note: endlessly means without its last letter

parts.note: an indie is an independent record label
ana is a collection of anecdotes and gossip about someone

explanation.surface: The condition of a record label that keeps attracting tittle-tattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like condition but is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A Midwestern member of the United States, capital Indianapolis.

clue.text: Raised from bed, picked up from here

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: an anchor is aweigh when just lifted clear of the sea bed

explanation.surface: Someone is hauled out of bed and collected from here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is the sea bed, not a sleeper's bed.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning at a distance or to another place, so not here.

clue.text: Quote from animated character who's put a CD out

indicators.note: out in the sense of not in order, so the letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A cartoon character's catchphrase coming from someone who released an album.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs Bunny's catchphrase from Warner Bros cartoons, said while munching a carrot.

clue.text: Note about period headgear

indicators.note: about means around, so the note goes round the period

parts.note: ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A memo about the hats of a historical period.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed felt hat with a double crown, worn in hot climates.

clue.text: Beliefs of the uninitiated prolonged speech

definitions.note: the answer is singular but names a whole set of beliefs

indicators.note: uninitiated means lacking an initial, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a screed is a long tedious speech or piece of writing

explanation.surface: Novices reveal their convictions in a long-winded address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uninitiated' looks like novices but signals losing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement of faith, a system of religious or other principles someone holds.

clue.text: Girl repelled Geordie with primitive instincts

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a Geordie is from Newcastle in the North East of England, NE
the id is Freud's term for the primitive instinctive part of the mind

explanation.surface: A girl was put off by a man from Newcastle with base urges.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a native of Tyneside, in the North East of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, as in the writer Blyton, so a girl.

clue.text: Browse ten gripping books, after exam certificate

indicators.note: after says the remaining pieces come later in the answer

parts.note: a dip, short for diploma, is an exam certificate

indicators.note: gripping means holding inside, so ten encloses the books

parts.note: IO looks like the figures 1 and 0, ten
NT is the New Testament, books of the Bible

explanation.surface: After getting a certificate, a student skims ten absorbing books.
explanation.definitionFit: To look through casually, sampling a book here and there.

clue.text: What, being retracted, is stuck in sullen alderman's throat

indicators.note: being retracted means drawn backwards, so the letters are read right to left
is stuck in says the word sits inside the clue words

explanation.surface: Something is lodged in a grumpy councillor's gullet.
explanation.definitionFit: A childish or humorous term for the gullet, the passage food goes down.

clue.text: Wood spirit no longer for drinking these days

parts.note: a dry person is teetotal, no longer drinking alcohol
AD, anno domini, refers to the present era

explanation.surface: Wood alcohol is not drinkable nowadays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood spirit' suggests methanol, but here it is a nymph.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, a nymph inhabiting trees and forests.

clue.text: Person milking crowds after backing charity

indicators.note: after backing means once turned backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a myriad is a vast number, crowds
aid is charity, help to those in need

explanation.surface: Someone exploits throngs after supporting a good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milking' looks like exploiting, but it is milking a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed in a farm's dairy, milking cows.
